For a single ordinary U.S. equity ETF, establish a **fund launch budget** and a separate **ongoing operating budget**; obtain platform, service-provider, and distribution terms rather than assuming a standard price.

**One-time / launch costs:** legal and tax structuring, registration and disclosure drafting, regulatory filing and exchange-listing costs, initial audit/setup, platform onboarding and integrations, index/data licensing setup, and launch marketing. Assign each cost to the sponsor or fund under the contracts and disclose any fund-paid organization/launch expenses and caps or reimbursements. The sponsor commonly bears expenses above any agreed fund cap.

**Recurring costs:** administration/accounting/NAV, custody, transfer agency, audit/tax, index/data licensing, listing and regulatory fees, platform or unitary servicing fee, and distribution/marketing. A unitary-fee arrangement generally has the sponsor pay the bundled operating expenses from its fee; specify exclusions, pass-throughs, caps, and who pays brokerage, portfolio transaction costs, and extraordinary expenses. Brokerage, spreads, and market impact are generally borne by the fund/shareholders, not included in the expense ratio.

**Seed assets are capital, not expenditure:** initial ETF shares/assets provide operating scale and facilitate trading; they remain fund assets, exposed to investment risk and subject to redemption, not a launch-cost line item.

Break-even is when retained sponsor revenue (unitary fee on average assets, net of waivers/rebates and platform/distribution shares) covers sponsor-borne fixed and variable costs. To earn a positive margin, revenue must exceed those costs—not merely equal them.
